subject.title: feat(skills): add option to disable ~/.agents/skills scanning for Claude Code coexistence

question: Should OpenClaw expose a public `skills.load` opt-out for built-in agent skill sources, and what exact config shape should own it?
rationale: The source-level behavior is real, but solving it adds public config surface and changes built-in skill-source semantics, which repository policy reserves for maintainer product/API judgment.

options.title: Add typed source-disable list
options.body: Expose a narrow list of supported built-in source ids such as `agents-skills-personal` and skip them consistently in discovery and watching.

options.title: Add personal-source toggle only
options.body: Limit the contract to disabling the personal `$HOME/.agents/skills` source and leave project `.agents/skills` always enabled.

options.title: Keep current convention
options.body: Reject a new config knob and keep AgentSkills compatibility always on, accepting per-skill disables as the only current workaround.

recommendation.title: Add typed source-disable list
recommendation.body: Expose a narrow list of supported built-in source ids such as `agents-skills-personal` and skip them consistently in discovery and watching.

likelyOwner.reason: The watcher/source-loading history makes this the strongest current routing candidate for the config-surface decision.
